query: Most of my money is in cash right now. Is that okay or should I shift it into investments?

recommendations.title: Maintain High Cash Position to Complete Emergency Fund
recommendations.summary: Keep majority of assets in cash until you reach your $22,000 emergency fund target, which should be your top priority given moderate debt and no current emergency fund.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $15,000 in cash (60% of $25,000), you're 68% of the way to your $22,000 emergency fund goal. Given your conservative risk tolerance (loss comfort of 3/10), moderate debt ($38,000), and lack of emergency fund, maintaining high cash reserves is appropriate. Your monthly expenses are $3,800, so you need approximately $22,800 for a true 6-month emergency fund. Only after securing this foundation should you consider increasing investment exposure. Your current cash position is a strength, not a weakness, given your financial situation and goals.
recommendations.suggested_action: Keep current cash allocation; continue directing savings to high-yield savings account until emergency fund is fully funded

recommendations.title: Maintain Conservative Investment Mix in VTTSX and BND
recommendations.summary: Your current 40% investment allocation in target-date fund and bonds is appropriately conservative for your risk profile and experience level.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your $10,000 in investments (30% VTTSX target-date fund, 10% BND bonds) represents a prudent allocation for a beginner investor with conservative risk tolerance. VTTSX (Vanguard Target Retirement 2065) provides automatic diversification and rebalancing, while BND offers stability. This mix is appropriate while you complete your emergency fund. Do not increase investment exposure until emergency reserves are secured and you've reduced debt burden. The target-date fund will automatically adjust risk as you age, making it ideal for your 5-7 year home purchase timeline.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold current positions; resume contributions only after emergency fund is complete

recommendations.title: Prioritize Debt Reduction After Emergency Fund Completion
recommendations.summary: With $38,000 in debt against $25,000 in assets, focus on debt paydown after securing emergency fund to improve net worth and reduce financial risk.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your negative net worth (-$13,000) and moderate debt level present financial risk that should be addressed before aggressive investing. After completing your emergency fund, direct surplus income toward debt reduction rather than increasing investment contributions. Depending on interest rates, paying down debt may provide better risk-adjusted returns than conservative investments. This approach aligns with your conservative risk tolerance and will strengthen your financial foundation for future home purchase. Once emergency fund is complete and high-interest debt is reduced, you can gradually increase investment contributions.
recommendations.suggested_action: Create debt paydown plan; allocate 50-70% of monthly surplus to debt after emergency fund is funded
recommendations.expected_return_range: Varies by debt interest rate (guaranteed return)

recommendations.title: Future Consideration: Add HYSA for House Down Payment Fund
recommendations.summary: Once emergency fund is complete, establish separate high-yield savings account specifically for your $60,000 house down payment goal in 5-7 years.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your $60,000 down payment goal requires a dedicated savings strategy separate from emergency funds and investments. Given the medium-term 5-7 year timeline and conservative risk tolerance, a combination of high-yield savings (for funds needed in years 1-3) and conservative investments like BND or short-term bond funds (for years 4-7) would be appropriate. This recommendation becomes actionable after your emergency fund is complete and debt is reduced. Start by saving $700-900 monthly in a HYSA to reach approximately $50,000-65,000 in 5-7 years, complemented by your existing VTTSX holdings for growth component.
recommendations.suggested_action: Implement after emergency fund complete: Open dedicated HYSA for house fund, contribute $700-900 monthly
